nodes.label: install.sh Modes
nodes.rationale: --install is the only mode that modifies the system, and it asks before adding a third-party PPA.

nodes.label: ~/.config Ownership Conflict
nodes.rationale: setup.py and home-manager both want to own ~/.config/hypr, and home-manager refuses to overwrite a symlink it did not create, so the old links must be removed first.

nodes.label: home-manager Configuration
nodes.rationale: Alternative to setup.py that manages the same ~/.config files but from pinned revisions, so another machine receives the same tools rather than whatever the distro ships that week.

nodes.label: Impure Activation (--impure)
nodes.rationale: --impure only allows reading $USER and $HOME: the two facts that differ between a VM, a laptop and a desktop. Package versions keep coming from flake.lock.

nodes.label: mkOutOfStoreSymlink
nodes.rationale: Default home-manager behaviour copies files read-only into /nix/store so every tweak needs a switch; out-of-store symlinks preserve the edit-in-place flow setup.py gave. Side effect: ~/.config follows the active git branch.

nodes.label: home.stateVersion 24.11
nodes.rationale: It is the release whose defaults this configuration was written against, not a desired version; changing it can silently alter behaviour.

nodes.label: Side-by-Side Nix Session
nodes.rationale: A compositor that does not start leaves you with no session to fix it from, so the Nix entry sits beside the distro entry under another name: a failed Nix session costs a logout, not the machine.

nodes.label: brave-browser Binary Name Divergence
nodes.rationale: The apt package installs brave-browser while the AUR package installs brave, so keysbindings.lua picks whichever exists instead of assuming one.

nodes.label: JetBrainsMono Nerd Font Requirement
nodes.rationale: Configs request a single family on purpose: three were requested before, two were missing, and rofi and hyprlock silently fell back to a default font. The Nerd Font variant is mandatory because the configs paint icon glyphs.

nodes.label: rofi Wayland Fork
nodes.rationale: Ubuntu's rofi is X11-only and does not work under Hyprland; because envs.lua puts ~/.nix-profile/bin first, the Nix 2.0.0 build wins and speaks Wayland natively via layer-shell.

nodes.label: Dependency Packaging Gap
nodes.rationale: The dotfiles need about 30 programs and the set of distros packaging all of them is empty; this directory is the honest map of that gap.

nodes.label: install.sh --verify-names
nodes.rationale: Turns guessed package names into a concrete list by listing everything the local package manager cannot resolve, without changing anything.

nodes.label: Command-Based Dependency Format
nodes.rationale: Package names differ per distro but the command the config invokes is the same everywhere; 'cmd_a/cmd_b' means either alternative satisfies the dependency.

nodes.label: Hyprland Dotfiles Repository
nodes.rationale: Desktop configuration repository for a Hyprland session (Lua config, waybar, rofi, dunst, wlogout, quickshell, btop); neovim deliberately lives in its own repository because it is the only piece worth installing standalone.

nodes.label: Two Exclusive Installation Paths
nodes.rationale: Nix and distro packages are alternatives, not layers: both want to own ~/.config, so the user must pick one.

nodes.label: setup.py --unlink Mode
nodes.rationale: Removes only symlinks pointing at this checkout, so real directories and links created by something else are left in place and reported; it is the required preliminary step before switching to home-manager.

nodes.label: Arch pacman Manifest
nodes.rationale: UNVERIFIED: written from the command list, never checked against a live Arch machine; run ./install.sh --verify-names on Arch to correct it.

nodes.label: Ubuntu PPA Manifest
nodes.rationale: PPAs are a third-party source of system packages, so install.sh asks before adding them.

nodes.label: Ubuntu 24.04 Manifest
nodes.rationale: Every name verified with apt-cache policy on a working 24.04 machine; fonts-jetbrains-mono is listed only because apt has no Nerd Font package, and the comment warns it is the unpatched font.

nodes.label: No Automatic AUR Installation
nodes.rationale: install.sh prints the AUR list instead of installing it and leaves the helper choice (paru, yay, makepkg) to the user, because an AUR helper builds and runs arbitrary upstream PKGBUILDs.

nodes.label: Debian Install Unproven
nodes.rationale: Names resolve in a debian:sid container, but a full apt-get install fails today because network-manager-gnome depends on network-manager-applet with no installable candidate; the rest is cascading fallout. Treated as name-correct and install-unproven until the test is finished.

nodes.label: No Power Keybinding Safety Rationale
nodes.rationale: MOD+Q closes the window, so putting shutdown on MOD+Shift+Q meant one stray Shift powered the machine off without asking; power actions moved into wlogout ordered least-to-most destructive.

nodes.label: Cyclic Renewal Metaphor
nodes.rationale: The unbroken loop expresses 'power cycle' / starting over, the conventional visual metaphor for reboot and the reason a circular arrow is used instead of a power-toggle symbol.

nodes.label: Power-Action Icon Family
nodes.rationale: The five icons in wlogout/icons share one visual language - monochrome white fill, thin dark keyline, transparent square canvas and tapering strokes - so the menu reads as a single coherent action row.

nodes.label: Restart / Reboot Action
nodes.rationale: Denotes a full system restart in the session power menu, deliberately distinct from the sibling shutdown, suspend, logout and lock actions.

nodes.label: White Fill with Thin Dark Keyline
nodes.norm_label: white fill with thin dark keyline
nodes.rationale: Solid white fill with a roughly 1px black outline: the white body dominates against dark session backgrounds while the keyline preserves the silhouette on light ones, and both can be recolored via the surrounding stylesheet.

nodes.label: wlogout Power Menu
nodes.rationale: wlogout is the Wayland logout/power launcher; this PNG is one of the per-action icon assets its buttons render, sitting beside lock, logout, shutdown and suspend.

nodes.label: Outlined Arrowhead at Lower Left
nodes.rationale: Hollow, keyline-only chevron terminating the sweep; it supplies the directional cue that turns a plain ring into a restart/refresh sign.

nodes.label: Circular Arrow Glyph
nodes.rationale: A nearly closed sweeping loop: the band leaves a pointed tail at bottom centre, runs up the right side, over the top and down the left side to an arrowhead at the lower left, reading as a counter-clockwise rotation rather than a static power symbol.

nodes.label: Reboot Icon
nodes.rationale: 512x512 RGBA power-action glyph for wlogout's reboot button: a white, taper-stroked circular arrow with a hairline black keyline on a transparent background, so it reads on the dark logout overlay and can be tinted by wlogout's CSS.

nodes.label: Tapered Brush-Style Band
nodes.rationale: The stroke is widest across the top and right arc and narrows to needle points at the bottom tail and the arrowhead, giving a hand-drawn calligraphic feel instead of a uniform-stroke line icon.

nodes.label: 512x512 Transparent Canvas
nodes.rationale: Full-bleed square art on an alpha background (about 16% opaque coverage, generous breathing room on all sides) with no baked-in label, sized to drop straight into wlogout's icon slot.

nodes.label: Media-Player Pause Convention
nodes.rationale: The twin-bar symbol is standardized by media transport controls; reusing it on a power menu relies on users already knowing it, trading literal depiction (e.g. a moon or a sleeping figure) for instant recognition.

nodes.label: wlogout Power-Menu Icon Family
nodes.rationale: The icons directory holds one icon per session action (lock, logout, suspend, hibernate, reboot, shutdown); this file is one member and inherits the family's shared circular, thin-stroke, transparent treatment.

nodes.label: System Suspend Action
nodes.rationale: The filename names the destination action: wlogout maps this asset to a suspend entry in its button layout, so the icon is content-addressed by command rather than by shape.

nodes.label: Theme-Neutral Recolorable Rendering
nodes.rationale: Because the strokes are near-neutral and the background is transparent, the widget's own background (dark overlay) supplies the contrast; this is what lets one asset sit on either a dark or light wlogout theme without editing the PNG.

nodes.label: wlogout Suspend Icon
nodes.rationale: 512x512 RGBA PNG used as the 'suspend' button artwork for the wlogout power menu; a single flat glyph on a transparent canvas so it composites over the blurred overlay without a baked-in background.

nodes.label: Enclosing Circular Ring
nodes.rationale: A single thin circular outline nearly touching the canvas edges, giving the glyph a contained badge silhouette that matches the other circular wlogout action icons.

nodes.label: Pause Glyph (Two Vertical Bars)
nodes.rationale: Two tall, rounded, evenly spaced vertical bars centered in the frame: the universal media 'pause' symbol, borrowed to mean 'suspend the machine' because the two states share the idea of halting without ending.

nodes.label: Transparent Square Canvas
nodes.rationale: Alpha channel is fully transparent outside the strokes, and the artwork is square with equal margins, so the icon scales cleanly at typical wlogout button sizes without clipping or letterboxing.

nodes.label: Monochrome Thin-Stroke Icon Style
nodes.rationale: Only two visual weights exist (outline ring and solid bars) with no gradients, shadows, or fills, keeping the icon legible at small sizes and visually consistent with line-art desktop theming.

nodes.label: Monochrome Outline Icon Style
nodes.rationale: Uniform hairline stroke, no fill, no gradient, perfectly black-on-transparent: the icons are meant to be recoloured at runtime by the wlogout/GTK theme, so the asset carries shape only and never colour or shading.

nodes.label: Log Out Action
nodes.rationale: The session action this asset triggers: terminate the current Hyprland/Wayland user session and return to the display manager, as opposed to locking (keep session alive), suspending/rebooting (power states) or shutting down.

nodes.label: Logout Icon (logout.png)
nodes.rationale: 512x512 transparent line-art icon used by wlogout as the 'logout' action tile in the session/power menu; a door frame with an arrow leaving it communicates 'leave this session' without text, so it reads at a glance on a blurred lockscreen background.

nodes.label: Rounded Door Frame Outline
nodes.rationale: Far-left rounded rectangle drawn as a single thin stroke with an open notch on its right edge; the gap is where the arrow exits, so the frame is deliberately incomplete rather than a closed box.

nodes.label: Rightward Exit Arrow
nodes.rationale: Horizontal shaft with a chevron head pointing right, breaking through the frame's opening; direction encodes 'out of here / end the session' and is what distinguishes logout from lock, reboot, shutdown and suspend icons that share the same visual family.

nodes.label: Transparent Background Asset
nodes.rationale: Alpha-only artwork with no backdrop or border, so the tile composites cleanly over wlogout's blurred Wayland wallpaper instead of showing an icon-sized opaque square.

nodes.label: envs.lua PATH Fix
nodes.rationale: Applies the PATH fix in the only layer that always runs, the compositor config itself, and computes the value from the inherited PATH so the same line is a no-op on a setup.py machine.

nodes.label: nixGL Wrapping
nodes.rationale: This is not NixOS: windowed programs were built against nixpkgs Mesa while kernel and drivers come from Ubuntu, so without nixGL they die at startup with a GL/EGL error.

nodes.label: Idempotent PATH Guard
nodes.rationale: env survives hyprctl reload, which re-reads the config; without the find() guard each reload stacked another copy of the prefix.

nodes.label: Child Process PATH Verification
nodes.rationale: Must inspect a child process environ, not Hyprland's own: /proc/<pid>/environ is a snapshot from exec time and does not reflect later setenv calls.

nodes.label: Session PATH Gap
nodes.rationale: The display manager execs /usr/bin/start-hyprland with no login shell in between, so ~/.profile is never read and hm-session-vars.sh never loads; anything that lives only in Nix fails at startup silently.

nodes.label: Emulated GPU Failure Mode
nodes.rationale: With QEMU stdvga/bochs (PCI 1234:1111) there is no /dev/dri/renderD128 and Mesa has no driver for that PCI, so Aquamarine finds no EGLDevice; the config is not at fault, the emulated GPU is.

nodes.label: hyprland-session.env Extension Point
nodes.rationale: Some variables must be set before Hyprland picks a renderer, which is before it reads any of its own config; VirtualBox needs LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 and the file is moved aside to .vm-backup outside a VM.

nodes.label: awww Fork of swww
nodes.rationale: nixpkgs renamed swww to awww and supplies both awww and awww-daemon; the hand-copied /usr/bin/swww binaries belong to no dpkg package and are dead weight under Nix.

nodes.label: Session PATH Gap (Manual)
nodes.rationale: Every manual entry installs into /usr/local/bin, ~/.local/bin or ~/.nix-profile/bin; none of those are in the session PATH because the display manager starts the compositor without a login shell. A half-started session is the symptom to recognise.

nodes.label: quickshell Wallpaper Picker
nodes.rationale: Now supplied only by Nix in ~/.nix-profile/bin, so the MOD+W shortcut depends on the PATH fix; the loose checkout in ~/Downloads no longer matters.

nodes.label: Unowned /usr/bin Binaries
nodes.rationale: Hand-copied binaries owned by no dpkg package will never be touched by an apt update and will not exist on a new machine.

nodes.label: local.lua Per-Machine Overrides
nodes.rationale: Git-ignored file loaded last so it overrides shared values; holds only what cannot be deduced (connector names, resolutions, scale, wallpaper, desktop-to-monitor pinning).

nodes.label: hyprshot Deliberately Excluded
nodes.rationale: hyprshot depends on hyprland, which drags Qt 6 through hyprland-qtutils: 640 MiB measured for a 60 KB screenshot script. It ships as a loose script in ~/.local/bin instead.

nodes.label: Install vs Launch Distinction
nodes.rationale: Installing a program and having the keybinding find it are two different problems; the PATH question decides whether any of it can be launched from the session at all.

nodes.label: Automatic Environment Detection
nodes.rationale: Anything deducible is deduced rather than configured, because a setting you must remember to place on every machine is a setting that will eventually be missing; this is what lets one commit run on laptop and desktop with no per-machine branch.

nodes.label: Neovim LazyVim Requirement
nodes.rationale: LazyVim needs a recent Neovim; Ubuntu 24.04 ships 0.9.x, so 0.11.6 comes from the official tarball/AppImage into ~/.local/bin.

nodes.label: install-hyprland-session
nodes.rationale: Registers the session entry where that machine's display manager will read it; needs root, so it is a separate one-time step and cannot be part of the activation. It detects the location instead of assuming it.

nodes.label: systemd display-manager.service Query
nodes.rationale: display-manager.service is an alias of whichever manager is enabled, and that answer holds equally on Ubuntu, Mint and Arch.

nodes.label: Session Registration Directory Detection
nodes.rationale: A fixed path would fail silently in the wrong directory: no error, no warning, just a session that is not listed. GDM reads /usr/local/share while SDDM and LightDM use explicit lists in their own config.

nodes.label: Rounded Lock Body
nodes.rationale: Squat, almost-square rounded rectangle that anchors the composition and is visibly heavier than the shackle, so the silhouette reads bottom-heavy and stable — the visual weight cue that says 'locked', complementing the arch above.

nodes.label: Padlock Glyph
nodes.rationale: The image's subject is a padlock: the universally understood 'locked' pictogram. A padlock rather than a keyhole, shield or key was chosen so the action is legible at tile size and distinguishable from the neighbouring logout, suspend, reboot and shutdown glyphs in the same power menu.

nodes.label: Screen Lock Action
nodes.rationale: The session action this asset triggers: lock the screen with the compositor's locker (swaylock/hyprlock) while keeping the running session and its processes alive — the distinction from logout (session ends) and suspend (power state changes).

nodes.label: U-Shaped Shackle
nodes.rationale: Domed arch rising from the body's shoulders, drawn as a thick white band with a hollow inner arch. The inner arch is negative space cut out of the filled silhouette, not a second outline, which is why the shape stays readable when the icon is shrunk to a menu tile.

nodes.label: wlogout Power Menu
nodes.rationale: The host interface: wlogout is a Wayland session/power menu that shows a grid of action buttons (lock, logout, suspend, hibernate, reboot, shutdown), each pairing an icon from wlogout/icons/ with a text label. This icon is the grid's lock tile and inherits the set's shared monochrome asset conventions.

nodes.label: Lock Icon (lock.png)
nodes.rationale: 512x512 RGBA icon used by wlogout as the 'lock' action tile: a solid white padlock silhouette on a transparent canvas, with the artwork bounding box at roughly (50,5)-(461,506) so the glyph fills the tile height and leaves even side padding. It carries shape only, no keyhole and no text, so the DE/WM theme decides its colour and the wallpaper shows through.

nodes.label: Filled White Silhouette Style
nodes.rationale: Artwork is a single flat opaque-white fill (255,255,255) with no stroke, gradient, shadow or shading; only anti-aliased edge pixels deviate. Solid fill was chosen over hairline strokes because thin lines vanish at small tile sizes; colour comes from the theme at runtime, keeping the asset a pure shape/mask.

nodes.label: Keyhole-Free Silhouette
nodes.rationale: Deliberate omission: a classic padlock would show a keyhole on the body, but this icon drops it so the body is one uninterrupted white mass. The detail would be lost at tile size and only adds visual noise, so recognition rests on the arch-plus-block outline alone.

nodes.label: Rounded-Corner Geometry
nodes.rationale: Soft, generously rounded corners on the body and a circular shackle arch — no sharp angles anywhere — matching the rounded visual language of the Wayland/WM theme instead of a hard-edged industrial lock icon.

nodes.label: 512x512 Canvas with Inset Artwork
nodes.rationale: Square 512x512 canvas with the glyph inset about 50 px from the left and right edges, so every icon in the wlogout set shares one optical size and the grid of tiles lines up without per-icon CSS offsets.

nodes.label: Transparent Background
nodes.rationale: The PNG is 8-bit RGBA with a fully transparent backdrop and no border or plate, so wlogout composites the glyph directly over its blurred Wayland wallpaper instead of showing an icon-sized opaque square.
